findings.decompiled: call address(ext_call.return_data[0]) with: args mem[mem[64] len ...]  (55 of 135 calls without a name, 38 argument lists as raw memory, 6 event payloads and 1 return as raw memory)
findings.source: NodeDelegator.sol:310-327 _getDelegationManager().queueWithdrawals(queuedWithdrawalParams); :355-397 completeQueuedWithdrawal(withdrawal, assets, receiveAsTokens), safeTransfer, receiveFromNodeDelegator{value}
findings.issue: After the first symbolic allocation (struct arrays, return-data-sized buffers) the calls to the DelegationManager, the unstaking vault and the tokens lose their names and arguments, and the WithdrawalQueued / EthTransferred events print their data as raw memory: the same free-memory-pointer self-alias as in the other contracts of this batch (P2).
findings.rule: mem[64] >= 0x80 on every path, so the selector store at mem[mem[64]] leaves mem[64] unchanged and the argument area folds to the stored words.

notes: All 30 ABI functions and the fallback/receive reviewed; no semantic error found. The large functions (completeUnstaking x2, initiateUnstaking, undelegate, getAssetUnstaking, verifyWithdrawalCredentials, stake32Eth*) by structure: role modifiers (LRTConfig role checks), pause and reentrancy guards, the withdrawal-staker / length / strategy-asset checks, balancesBefore via getBalances, the receiveAsTokens branch with ETH vs ERC20 transfers, uncompleted-withdrawal accounting, events. Source loops (7): undelegate's root loop, initiateUnstaking's strategy check, completeUnstaking's validation and transfer loops, getAssetUnstaking's two nested loops, getBalances: all whiles. Implicit: ABI decoding of the Withdrawal / proof parameters and encoding of QueuedWithdrawalParams[] (nested arrays) for the DelegationManager (11 plain copies, P7). HashStorage / UnlockedWithdrawalsInitializer loops belong to other contracts.
summary: Faithful with all 7 source loops shown as whiles; as elsewhere, the EigenLayer and vault calls after the first symbolic allocation lose their names and arguments because of the free-memory-pointer aliasing assumption.
